title: Fix the untraced-records report
prompt: The tracing team wants the log records that were written without a trace id. The report below also lists rows with no id, level or service at all. Fix `solve(application_logs_raw)`.
rules: Return `log_id`, `level` and `service`, all text, for every record whose `trace_id` is null or missing.
A line that isn't valid JSON isn't a record, so it never appears. A record with no `log_id` is still a record.
hints: Look at the rows with nothing in them: which lines of the file did they come from?
In the default mode a broken line still becomes a row, with every field NULL, so it passes a NULL check on `trace_id`.
Read with `mode="DROPMALFORMED"` so broken lines are left out before you look for missing trace ids.
starter:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F


def solve(application_logs_raw):
    path = "/tmp/logs/export"
    application_logs_raw.write.mode("overwrite").text(path)
    schema = "log_id STRING, level STRING, service STRING, trace_id STRING"
    logs = spark.read.json(path, schema=schema)
    return logs.filter(F.col("trace_id").isNull()).select("log_id", "level", "service")
explanation: A missing field and a broken line both end up as NULL, but they aren't the same thing. With the default `PERMISSIVE` mode, each broken line becomes a row whose fields are all NULL, so `trace_id` is NULL there too and the filter lets it through. Add `mode="DROPMALFORMED"` to the read and the broken lines are gone before the filter; a record that simply has no `trace_id`, or `"trace_id": null`, is valid JSON and stays. Filtering on `log_id` being present instead looks right on the sample but also drops a real record that has no id. Reading without a schema and checking `_corrupt_record` fails on a file with no broken lines, because Spark only adds that column when it finds one.
